title: Pack six biscuit packs off a moving belt into two cases before the red line, letting the two cracked packs pass
instruction: Take the six good biscuit packs off the moving belt before they cross the red line and put one in each cell of the two cases. Let the cracked packs with the red band ride past.
context: Hand packers on food lines take products off a moving belt into cases at the pace of the line, and let damaged ones pass to the reject end. Here a pack passes every 1.7 seconds, faster than one arm's pick-and-place cycle of about 4 seconds, so the two arms have to share the line.
setup: Station table; distances from the arm bases' line are forward, and left or right from the point midway between the arms. A black rubber belt 12 cm wide, its top 3 cm above the table, runs left to right across the table, centred 33 cm forward. It runs from 108 cm right of the midpoint, past the table's edge, to 45 cm left of it, with low steel side rails 8 mm wide and a steel end stop at its left end. Its surface moves right to left at 6 cm/s from the start of the trial. Eight foil-wrapped biscuit packs ride on the belt in one line, each 4 cm across the belt, 7 cm along it and 3.5 cm tall, 50 g, gold, handled as rigid. The leading pack's centre starts 30 cm right of the midpoint, and the others follow at 10 cm centre to centre, so a pack passes any point every 1.7 seconds. The third and sixth packs in line are cracked, each marked with a red band 3 cm wide across its top. A small red line on the table just beyond the belt, 24 cm left of the midpoint, marks the line. Two open cases are fixed to the table, centred 15 cm forward and 17 cm right and left of the midpoint. Each has a 4 mm card floor and steel walls 4 mm thick and 2 cm tall, and three cells in a row front to back, each 7.5 cm front to back and 10.5 cm left to right.
scoring: A pack is in a cell when its centre is inside the cell, it is within 10 degrees of flat, and its underside is within 6 mm of its case's floor, so a pack up on a wall doesn't count. A pack is lost once it crosses the red line while on the belt, or if it moves slower than 2 cm/s on the belt for 3 seconds, which rules out holding packs back; a lost pack earns nothing even if it is packed later. 1.0 if each of the six cells holds exactly one good pack that was never lost, both cracked packs are past the red line, and the packed packs stay still for 1 second. Otherwise, at the end: 0.15 for each cell holding exactly one good pack that was never lost, less 0.3 if a cracked pack is in a case, never below 0. In a real trial, a photo from above shows which pack is in which cell, a tape measure checks a pack that may be up on a wall, and a video shows the red line and any held-back pack.
reset_notes: Stop the belt, set the eight packs back in line at their marks, and start the belt with the trial; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Packs are rigid, where real foil packs give a little. The belt is a fixed slab whose surface carries what rests on it, with no rollers or belt stretch, and it runs on CPU physics (-E device=cpu), because packs fall through it on GPU physics. Missed packs collect at the end stop. Nothing is deformable.
